items.title: She Taught the Macintosh to Smile
items.summary: The Macintosh didn’t always smile. Susan Kare gave it one — and with a handful of black pixels, helped transform the computer from an intimidating machine into something that felt human. More than 40 years later, we’re still speaking the visual language she helped create.

items.title: Web-Perf Wednesday 013 – CrUX Adds Soft-Navigation Core Web Vitals
items.summary: CrUX adds experimental Core Web Vitals for SPA soft navigations, while Firefox and Safari improve cache evidence, image delivery, and rendering.

items.title: The Death of the Portfolio (And What to Do Before You’re Left Behind)
items.summary: A polished portfolio used to get you hired. Now AI makes polished work cheap, and clients want proof you can solve problems, communicate clearly, and deliver today.

items.title: Redefining My Relationship With You
items.summary: I no longer knew how to define my relationship with the people who read my work. Not teacher and student, not leads and customers. Here's where I eventually settled: fellow wayfarers.

items.title: Web Design Schools Have a Giant YouTube University Problem — And AI Just Made It Worse
items.summary: A web design degree used to be the obvious way to learn the craft. Now it’s competing with YouTube, AI, and people who spend those same years actually building things — so if universities can’t offer something better, students have every right to ask what they’re paying for.

items.title: Web-Perf Wednesday 012 – Return to the Unresolved Trace
items.summary: A quiet week leaves room to revisit unfinished performance investigations and turn partial evidence into a clear next step.

items.title: Web Designers Love Dark Mode Toggles. Users Might Not Care.
items.summary: Dark mode toggles are everywhere, but do users actually need them, or are designers designing for other designers? A growing UX debate is questioning whether that little sun-and-moon button deserves permanent space in your website’s header.
